title: Publish workflows must share a concurrency group keyed on the resource, not github.run_id
answers: release image pushes running concurrently or out of order
two release label updates overlap for the same release tag
how do I serialize a GitHub Actions workflow so publishes do not race
concurrency group per run does not serialize anything
body:
Symptom: Release image pushes or release label updates for the same release can run at the same time, so a publish can interleave with another and leave partial state.
Root cause: .github/workflows/push-images.yml, .github/workflows/update-release-labels.yml and .github/workflows/preview-docs.yml had `concurrency.group: ${{ github.run_id }}`, which is unique per run, so no two runs ever share a group and nothing is serialized.
Fix pattern: Key the group on the thing being published: `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}` for image pushes; `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.ref }}` for label updates, where manual runs have no release and fall back to the ref.
Constraints: Keep `cancel-in-progress: false` on publish workflows so an in-flight publish completes. Reviewers noted GitHub keeps only one pending run per group even with cancel-in-progress false, so more than two queued runs for one key can still drop a pending run.
applies: Any GitHub Actions workflow under .github/workflows/ that publishes or mutates shared release or deployment state.
says: Publishing container images for the same version runs simultaneously and leaves broken deployment state.
Simultaneous updates to release tags are stepping on each other and leaving mismatched version labels.
Preview builds for documentation triggered at the same time overwrite each other instead of waiting.
Ensure publishing jobs for identical release versions finish sequentially instead of clashing concurrently.
Prevent active release publishes from being cancelled when another update is queued for that release.
search: Workflows that publish or mutate release or deployment state must serialize execution by keying the concurrency group on the published resource rather than github.run_id. Applies to .github/workflows/push-images.yml using ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}, .github/workflows/update-release-labels.yml using ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.release.tag_name || github.ref }}, and .github/workflows/preview-docs.yml. Workflows must retain cancel-in-progress: false so in-flight publishes complete, though GitHub will drop runs if more than two are queued for a single key.
